newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Timan Pechora oil deal at standstill-source.
newsitem.headline: Russia Timan Pechora oil deal at standstill-source.

text.p: Talks between Russia and members of the Timan-Pechora international oil consortium have ground to a halt over differences on how to value parts of the $40 billion project, a source involved in the talks said on Friday.
"The talks have ground to a halt," said the source, who nonetheless added he hoped a deal could be reached by 1997.

He said Western members of the Timan-Pechora Co (TPC) were at odds with Russian participants over a host of issues, including how to value exploration and drilling done in recent years by Russia's Arkhangelskgeodobycha, part of the consortium.

TPC includes U.S. majors Exxon Corp, Amoco Corp and Texaco Inc, Norsk Hydro ASA of Norway and Russia's Rosneft in a project to tap 360 million tonnes of crude oil in Russia's Timan-Pechora basin in the remote north.

"There are a many sticking points in the talks and both sides have to meet half way," the source said. "Most of the quarrels centre around how to value things, for example, the work that has already been done on the project."
He said TPC President Tom Hazen had left Moscow but that talks could recommence in two weeks.
"Both sides need time to examine more deeply what their approaches to all this will be," he said. "We will need to search for non-standard solutions."
